subject.title: [security] Azure cleanup can delete matching-tag VMs without an exact local lease claim

question: Should Azure cleanup fail closed unless an exact local Azure lease claim matches the candidate before any destructive provider deletion?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but changing cleanup behavior for lost-local-state scenarios and destructive Azure resources should be owned as a security-boundary decision.

options.title: Require exact Azure claims
options.body: Treat this as a security-boundary bug and require a matching local claim before Azure cleanup deletes any VM or companion resource.

options.title: Keep tag/live checks only
options.body: Accept the current provider-side metadata model despite docs and VISION.md saying labels and IDs alone are not ownership proof.

options.title: Split reclaim policy first
options.body: Pause the fix until maintainers define an explicit Azure reclaim/adoption workflow for operators who intentionally lost local state.

recommendation.title: Require exact Azure claims
recommendation.body: Treat this as a security-boundary bug and require a matching local claim before Azure cleanup deletes any VM or companion resource.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the affected Azure cleanup implementation and nearby AWS exact-claim/security-boundary code in the available history.
